title: Pipeline: Update check_static.py to run on Windows too
description:
The purpose of this MR is similar to !23460

To eliminate minor syntax, spelling and similar bugs locally instead of finding them when the gitlab pipeline fails (again and again) we can use `tools/check_dissector.py` or a single tool like `check_static.py` for that matter.

However, `tools/check_static.py` can only be executed on Linux.

The proposed changes allow the script to be executed on Windows too.

**Note**, I was not able to test it on a Linux machine.

Still seems to work.  Amazingly, we have one issue each :smile: 

./tools/check_static.py | grep -v "in header"

Examining:
All dissector modules

Note: epan/dissectors/packet-oran.c  (0000000000002200 D dl_compression_options) is not referred to so could be static?

Note: epan/dissectors/packet-qcdiag.c  (0000000000000be0 D qcdiag_logcfg_ops_ext) is not referred to so could be static?

2157 issues found

On Windows I have zero issues shown.

That is weird :smile: 

Perhaps MSVC....

(it does not work for me without --build-folder)

```
tools\check_static.py --build-folder ..\wsbuild64
Examining:
All dissector modules

0 issues found
```

But qcdiag_logcfg_ops_ext is used in line [1177](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/epan/dissectors/packet-qcdiag.c?ref_type=heads#L1177):

`text = val_to_str_ext(pinfo->pool, operation, &qcdiag_logcfg_ops_ext, "Unknown Operation (0x%02x)");`

Yes, you need --build-folder.  I selfishly made it default to using ../wireshark_build which is where I usually build.

So qcdiag_logcfg_ops_ext is only used in packet-qcdiag.c, so it can be static as it is not currently shared with any other modules.  I believe this is worth doing to avoid:
- accidental merging of variables between modules
- exposing lots of private symbols from the library the dissectors are linked into

Also, if a symbol isn't referred to at all - even in that module - making it static will cause the build to fail, because that variable or function really is just wasting space (maybe the compiler would optimize it out, I don't know).

Above, I piped the output through 'grep -v "in header"', because a lot of dissectors declare symbols in a header file, but then nothing ever shares it, so it might as well not be in the header file and be static.  There are some functions that only ever get called from private dissectors, e.g.,

./tools/check_static.py --file epan/dissectors/packet-pdcp-lte.c

Examining:
epan/dissectors/packet-pdcp-lte.c

Note: epan/dissectors/packet-pdcp-lte.c  (0000000000003ac0 T set_pdcp_lte_up_ciphering_key) is not referred to so could be static? (declared in header but not referred to)

1 issues found

yes, I see now, I will correct it with the next MR, I need to add `static` indeed:

`static value_string_ext qcdiag_logcfg_ops_ext = VALUE_STRING_EXT_INIT(qcdiag_logcfg_ops);`

the problem seems to be about the location and the name of the object file.

I use `wsbuild64` folder name.

My command (from the wireshark folder):

`tools\check_static.py --build-folder ..\wsbuild64`

for example the script tries:

`...\wireshark-build\epan\dissectors\CMakeFiles\dissectors.dir\packet-yami.c.obj`

But it is actually

`...\wsbuild64\epan\dissectors\dissectors.dir\Release\packet-yami.obj`

Note the filename, the `.c` is not there when MSVC used.

okay, new version is provided. I have tested the folders and for me with MSVC it finds now all the *.obj files required. The `dumpbin.exe` has output so it works but at the end it does not find any issue like it found for you on Linux. This must be MSVC flags and/or `dumpbin.exe` issue, I think the script is OK.

I checked this new version - linux still works.  I'm happy to merge this as it is - I suspect that there is a semantic difference between what we understand from nm and dumpbin.exe output, which I can look into at some point.

Thanks again

yes, so there are two open issues which take time to further improve:

2. Analyze the `dumpbin.exe` output vs `nm` output to understand why there is nothing found on Windows while issues can be seen on Linux

Please proceed to merge it.
